answer: In a grove of trading agents, each identity must lock a marble-sized bond in escrow before it can vote on a shared ledger. Voting weight is proportional to the bond, so splitting funds across fake identities buys no extra influence. If an agent signs conflicting votes for the same ledger vertex, anyone can submit both signatures as proof and trigger loss of its bond. An attacker must therefore acquire and lock more capital to gain influence, and risks losing it by equivocating.
